questions.q: What single fact drives LTV's decision to use two primary ledgers instead of one?
options: The two entities are in different time zones
The two entities have different statutory currencies (USD and CAD)
Oracle Fusion limits each legal entity to one business unit
The two entities use different chart of accounts structures
questions.explain: A primary ledger has exactly one currency. Because the US parent reports in USD and the Canadian subsidiary in CAD, each needs its own primary ledger.

questions.q: How many legal entities, primary ledgers, and business units does the worked design use?
options: One legal entity, one ledger, two business units
Two legal entities, one shared ledger, two business units
Two legal entities, two primary ledgers, two business units
Two legal entities, two primary ledgers, one shared business unit
questions.explain: The design is a clean one-to-one stack: two legal entities, each with its own primary ledger and its own business unit.

questions.q: What do the US and Canadian primary ledgers share, even though their currency and legal entity differ?
options: Nothing — they are fully independent
The same chart of accounts structure and the same calendar
The same bank accounts
The same business unit
questions.explain: Sharing chart of accounts structure and calendar across both ledgers is what makes consolidated reporting across the two entities possible.

questions.q: Why is a single ledger holding both legal entities rejected as a shortcut?
options: Oracle Fusion technically cannot support more than one legal entity per ledger under any circumstances
Multiple legal entities under one ledger requires a shared ledger currency, which LTV's entities don't have
It would require deleting the Canadian subsidiary's legal entity record
It would prevent the US entity from using USD
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion does allow multiple legal entities per ledger, but only when they share the ledger's currency — which isn't true for LTV's USD parent and CAD subsidiary.

questions.q: A business unit is tied to how many primary ledgers?
options: Exactly one
Exactly two, one per currency
As many as the company has legal entities
Zero — business units are independent of ledgers
questions.explain: A business unit always references exactly one primary ledger, which is why two ledgers naturally produce two business units in this design.
